astro.summary:
Current stable Astro (2026-11-19): astro 7.4.13 (npm `latest`), requires Node >=22.23.4. Astro 6.0 shipped 2026-03-10 (CSP stable as `security.csp`, Fonts API stable as `fonts`, Live Collections, Zod 4 via `astro/zod`, Node 22+, Vite 7). Astro 7.0 shipped 2026-06-22 (Vite 8/Rolldown, Rust .astro compiler with stricter parsing, Rust markdown pipeline "Sätteri", Advanced Routing src/fetch.ts, route caching stable, 15–61% faster builds). Install today: `npm create astro@latest` → astro ^7.4.x.
i18n: `i18n: { locales: ['fr','en'], defaultLocale: 'fr', routing: { prefixDefaultLocale: false } }` serves FR at root (src/pages/*.astro) and EN under /en/ (src/pages/en/*). prefixDefaultLocale defaults to false; Astro does NO Accept-Language detection and no redirect in this mode (redirectToDefaultLocale only applies when prefixDefaultLocale: true).
Content: src/content.config.ts, `glob({ pattern, base })` from 'astro/loaders', `z` from 'astro/zod' (Zod 4; `astro:content` z export removed in 6), colocated cover via `schema: ({ image }) => z.object({ cover: image() })`.
Images: Sharp default service strips ALL metadata (EXIF/GPS) on every processed output — confirmed behavior, opt-in preservation still only a roadmap discussion (#1251). Default output .webp; `<Picture formats={['avif','webp']}>`; `layout` prop (constrained/full-width/fixed/none) auto-generates srcset/sizes; `widths`/`densities` for manual srcset. public/ files are copied verbatim — NOT stripped.
CSP: stable since 6.0 — `security: { csp: true }` hashes all bundled scripts/styles (SHA-256 default) and emits a <meta http-equiv> on static pages; 7.1 added script-src-elem/attr + style-src-elem/attr support. Zero-inline guarantee: `build.inlineStylesheets: 'never'` (default 'auto' inlines <4kb styles) + `vite.build.assetsInlineLimit: 0` (Astro inlines small scripts by default).
Sitemap: @astrojs/sitemap 3.7.6 — `sitemap({ i18n: { defaultLocale, locales } })` emits xhtml:link hreflang alternates; must be configured in the integration (not inherited from Astro i18n).
Fonts: Fonts API STABLE since 6.0 — top-level `fonts` key, `fontProviders.local()`, files copied to _astro/fonts (immutable caching), auto fallback generation, `<Font cssVariable preload />`; fully self-hosted = CNIL/GDPR-safe.
Dev-only page: no built-in flag (roadmap #1188 open); use rest-param route with `getStaticPaths()` returning `[]` when `import.meta.env.PROD`, or a tiny integration that `injectRoute()`s only when `command === 'dev'`.
risks: Astro 7's Rust compiler is stricter than 5.x/6.x tutorials assume: unclosed tags and unterminated attributes are build ERRORS, no longer silently fixed; most online snippets predate this.
Zod import changed in Astro 6: `import { z } from 'astro/zod'` (Zod 4). Old `import { z } from 'astro:content'` examples break.
Fonts API syntax changed between experimental (5.x: provider: 'local', top-level variants) and stable (6+: fontProviders.local(), options.variants) — copy only 6/7-era snippets.

Default build inlines small CSS (<4kb, inlineStylesheets:'auto') AND small scripts into the HTML — a 'self'-only CSP header will break the site unless you set build.inlineStylesheets:'never' and vite.build.assetsInlineLimit:0, or use security.csp hashes. The assetsInlineLimit:0 script-inlining kill-switch is the long-documented mechanism but the current scripts guide no longer names the config explicitly — verify with one test build (view-source should show zero <style>/<script> without src).

security.csp on a no-adapter static build delivers CSP as a <meta> tag: frame-ancestors, report-uri and sandbox are ignored in meta — those must be real HTTP headers at the host anyway. Hash-based CSP in a host-managed static header also means re-deploying headers whenever any inlined asset changes — prefer the zero-inline approach for host-level headers.

Static demos under public/demos/<slug>/ bypass Astro entirely: their inline scripts/styles are NOT hashed by security.csp and their images are NOT EXIF-stripped — sanitize them manually or scope per-path CSP headers at the host.
EXIF/GPS stripping only applies to Sharp-processed outputs (Image/Picture/getImage). Anything in public/ or linked as an original file keeps its metadata (relevant for French privacy posture).
@astrojs/sitemap does not read defineConfig({ i18n }) — hreflang locales must be duplicated in the sitemap() options and kept in sync with the i18n block.
Node >=22.23.4 required by astro 7.4.13 — check CI/host build images.
Minor source conflict: third-party posts date Astro 6 at 2026-02-10; the official blog says 2026-03-10 — trust astro.build.

cloudflare.summary:
1) Cloudflare officially steers NEW projects to Workers with static assets, not Pages. Banner on the Pages docs homepage: "Workers supports most Pages use cases and offers a broader feature set. It is Cloudflare's primary platform for building applications. Start new projects with Workers." Static-asset requests are free on Workers, and _headers/_redirects are supported natively.
2) Git integration = "Workers Builds": connect a GitHub repo, auto build+deploy on push; PRs/non-production branches get "Previews" with a stable per-branch URL <preview-name>-<worker-name>.<subdomain>.workers.dev plus an immutable per-deployment URL; Cloudflare posts the preview URL as a PR comment/check. Previews require Wrangler >= 4.135.0 (`npx wrangler preview` as the deploy command for branches).
3) _headers: multi-line blocks ([url] then indented "Name: value"); when MULTIPLE rules match one URL, the request "will inherit all rules' headers" (values joined with commas — fatal for CSP since combined CSPs intersect to the stricter policy). The documented fix is the detach syntax "! Header-Name": in a later /demos/* block, "! Content-Security-Policy" removes the CSP added by an earlier /* block, then you re-add the demo-specific CSP. Order matters: "Rules are applied in the order they appear in the file" and "! removes only what earlier rules have already added". Limits: 100 header rules max, 2,000 characters max per line.
4) Static-asset defaults: "Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate" + ETag (file hash) + CF-Cache-Status; edge-cached with tiered caching. _headers overrides these; docs' own example for fingerprinted assets: "Cache-Control: public, max-age=31556952, immutable"; keep the default (max-age=0, must-revalidate) for HTML.
5) Email Routing is receive/forward-only (outbound = separate "Email Service" product). Enabling it auto-adds MX records (Cloudflare routing MX servers, priorities auto-assigned) + TXT SPF "v=spf1 include:_spf.mx.cloudflare.net ~all" at the root. No user DKIM needed — Cloudflare signs forwarded mail itself (selector cf2024-1._domainkey) and uses SRS. For a domain that never sends: KEEP the Email Routing SPF include (do not use "v=spf1 -all"), and publish _dmarc TXT "v=DMARC1; p=reject;" — safe because DMARC only governs mail claiming From: your domain.
6) Cloudflare Registrar does NOT support .fr (absent from the official TLD list as of 2026-11-19; community threads confirm no timeline). Register with an AFNIC-accredited registrar and use Cloudflare DNS (free, full setup). AFNIC applies "diffusion restreinte" (WHOIS anonymization) BY DEFAULT to natural persons on .fr — automatic at registry level, registrar-independent. DNSSEC: enable in Cloudflare dashboard (DNS > Settings > Enable DNSSEC), then manually add the DS record at the external .fr registrar.
7) Mentions légales (hébergeur): Cloudflare, Inc., 101 Townsend St., San Francisco, CA 94107, USA — phone +1 (650) 319-8930 (both from the official privacy policy). French entity also listed there: Cloudflare France SAS, 6 place de la Madeleine, 75008 Paris. DPO: dpo@cloudflare.com.
cloudflare.details:
== 1. Workers vs Pages ==
Official guidance banner at the top of https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/ (verified live 2026-11-19): "Workers supports most Pages use cases and offers a broader feature set. It is Cloudflare's primary platform for building applications. Start new projects with Workers." Pages still functions (Git integration, 500 deploys/month on Free) but is in maintenance positioning. Migration guide https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/migration-guides/migrate-from-pages/ confirms: "_headers and _redirects files are supported natively in Workers with static assets" and static-asset requests remain free.

Minimal static-site Worker config (wrangler.jsonc, no Worker script needed):
{
  "name": "portfolio",
  "compatibility_date": "2026-11-19",
  "assets": { "directory": "./public" }
}

== 2. Git integration (Workers Builds) ==
https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/builds/ : "The Cloudflare Git integration lets you connect a new or existing Worker to a repository hosted by GitHub or GitLab, enabling automated builds and deployments for your Worker on push." Production branch pushes -> build + deploy new version. Non-production branches / PRs -> "Previews" (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/previews/): "Previews give each branch an isolated, production-like environment under the same Worker." Two URL kinds: Preview URL `<preview-name>-<worker-name>.<subdomain>.workers.dev` (always latest for the branch — this is the stable PR link) and Deployment URL `<deployment-id>-<worker-name>.<subdomain>.workers.dev` (immutable). GitHub integration (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/builds/git-integration/github-integration/): check runs per commit, PR comment listing "URLs for every host enabled for Previews"; "Subsequent pushes to the same branch update the same Preview URL." Branch deploy command: `npx wrangler preview` (Wrangler >= 4.135.0 required); production: `npx wrangler deploy`. Cloudflare recommends limiting the GitHub App scope to only the repos being built.

== 3. _headers (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/) ==
Place a plain-text `_headers` file at the ROOT of the static asset directory (it is parsed, never served). Syntax:
[url-or-pattern]
  Header-Name: value
Patterns support splats (/*) and can include host. COMBINATION SEMANTICS: "An incoming request which matches multiple rules' URL patterns will inherit all rules' headers" — e.g. a /static/styles.css request matching both /static/* and /* gets BOTH rules' headers; same-named headers are joined into one comma-separated value ("joining two rules produces conflicting directives" warning for Cache-Control). For CSP this is destructive: two CSPs enforce their intersection (strictest wins), so demos would inherit the strict site CSP.
DETACH syntax (confirmed in docs): prepend "! " — "This can be done by prepending the header name with an exclamation mark and space (! )." Ordering rules: "Rules are applied in the order they appear in the file." and "Because rules are applied in file order, ! removes only what earlier rules have already added." Therefore the guaranteed-single-CSP pattern is:

/*
  Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'
  X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
  Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
  Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()

/demos/*
  ! Content-Security-Policy
  Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:

(The /demos/* block MUST come after /* in the file.) Docs show the identical pattern with Cache-Control:
/assets/*
  Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, s-maxage=86400
/assets/model.bin
  ! Cache-Control
  Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800
LIMITS (verbatim): "You may define up to 100 header rules." / "Each line in the _headers file has a 2,000 character limit. The entire line, including spacing, header name, and value, counts towards this limit."

== 4. Caching defaults ==
Defaults served on every static asset (same docs page): Content-Type (inferred from extension at upload), "Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate", ETag (= hash of the file, honored via If-None-Match), CF-Cache-Status. Edge: "Cloudflare automatically caches static assets across its network" with tiered caching (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/). _headers overrides the defaults. Recommended setup: hashed/fingerprinted assets -> "Cache-Control: public, max-age=31556952, immutable" (docs' own example value, ~1 year); HTML -> leave the default max-age=0, must-revalidate (ETag makes revalidation cheap). Note: because of combining semantics, if /* already sets Cache-Control, use "! Cache-Control" before re-setting it in a narrower rule.

== 5. Email Routing ==
Receive/forward only; outbound sending is the separate "Email Service"/Email Sending product (https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-routing/, /email-routing/postmaster/). Setup wizard auto-creates DNS (https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-routing/setup/email-routing-dns-records/): MX records at @ -> "Cloudflare routing MX servers", priorities "Assigned automatically by Cloudflare" (docs do not hardcode hostnames; the dashboard inserts route1/route2/route3.mx.cloudflare.net); TXT at @: "v=spf1 include:_spf.mx.cloudflare.net ~all". Destination mailbox (e.g. personal Gmail) must be verified by clicking a confirmation email. DKIM: nothing for the user to publish — Cloudflare signs forwarded mail with its own keys ("Email Routing adds two DKIM signatures: one for email.cloudflare.net... and one for the recipient domain", selector cf2024-1._domainkey) and rewrites the envelope sender via SRS. Incoming mail: "Email Routing honors the DMARC and SPF policies published by the claimed sender's domain." For a domain that NEVER sends: keep the Email Routing SPF exactly as provided (replacing it with "v=spf1 -all" is only for domains with no mail at all — here the include is required), and publish TXT at _dmarc: "v=DMARC1; p=reject;" (optionally + "rua=mailto:contact@domain" for reports). This is safe with forwarding because your DMARC applies only to messages whose From: is your domain; Email Service docs confirm Cloudflare itself defaults to p=reject when onboarding a domain with no DMARC record, with the standard none->quarantine->reject ramp only needed if other services send as the domain.

== 6. Registrar / .fr ==
.fr is NOT in the official supported-TLD list at https://www.cloudflare.com/tld-policies/ (checked live; Registrar supports 400+ TLDs but no .fr), and Cloudflare community threads confirm no timeline. Practical setup: register the .fr at an AFNIC-accredited registrar (OVHcloud, Gandi, etc.), then add the domain to Cloudflare as a free "full setup" zone (change nameservers at the registrar). AFNIC WHOIS privacy: "diffusion restreinte" is applied BY DEFAULT to private individuals (natural persons) — AFNIC has anonymized WHOIS data by default for individuals on .fr since 2006 (AFNIC data publication and access policy, afnic.fr PDF) — so no paid WHOIS privacy is needed and it does not depend on the registrar. DNSSEC (https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dnssec/): dashboard -> DNS -> Settings -> "Enable DNSSEC", then add the displayed DS record at the registrar (manual, since the domain is not on Cloudflare Registrar; AFNIC supports DNSSEC). FYI the auto-DS path ("Cloudflare automatically adds DS records for domains using Cloudflare Registrar or those using .ch and .cz top-level domains", via CDS/CDNSKEY scanning, 1-2 days) does not apply to .fr.

== 7. Hébergeur for mentions légales (LCEN art. 6) ==
From the official privacy policy (https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/): "Cloudflare, Inc. 101 Townsend St. San Francisco, CA 94107" — phone +1 (650) 319-8930. The policy also lists "Cloudflare France SAS 6 place de la Madeleine 75008 Paris" (no phone given for the French entity; the service contract for Workers/Pages is with Cloudflare, Inc., so cite Cloudflare, Inc. as the host, optionally mentioning the French establishment). Contact emails: dpo@cloudflare.com, privacyquestions@cloudflare.com. Suggested wording: "Hébergeur : Cloudflare, Inc., 101 Townsend St., San Francisco, CA 94107, États-Unis — Tél. : +1 (650) 319-8930 — www.cloudflare.com".
risks: CSP combination trap: without '! Content-Security-Policy' in the /demos/* block, both the /* CSP and the demos CSP are applied and browsers enforce their intersection (strictest), silently breaking demos. The /demos/* block must appear AFTER /* in _headers because '!' only removes what earlier rules added.
_headers line limit is 2,000 characters INCLUDING the header name and indentation — a very long site-wide CSP plus a long demo CSP must each stay under this per-line cap; 100 rules max total.

Default Cache-Control on Workers static assets is max-age=0, must-revalidate — fine for HTML but you must explicitly add immutable rules for hashed assets; conversely, if /* sets Cache-Control you need '! Cache-Control' before overriding in narrower rules (values otherwise concatenate into conflicting directives).

Workers Previews require the branch build command to be 'npx wrangler preview' and Wrangler >= 4.135.0; preview/version URLs live on workers.dev and are disabled if workers_dev is disabled — avoid hardcoding the production origin in demo code/CSP that must also work on previews.
Pages still works today but Cloudflare explicitly says 'Start new projects with Workers' — picking Pages for a new 2026 site means building on a platform no longer receiving new features.

Email Routing: do NOT publish 'v=spf1 -all' (the generic no-mail-domain advice) — Email Routing requires 'v=spf1 include:_spf.mx.cloudflare.net ~all'. DMARC p=reject is safe and recommended since the domain never sends From: itself.
Email Routing is receive-only: replying FROM contact@domain requires a separate sending service (e.g. Gmail 'send as' with third-party SMTP) — out of scope of Email Routing.

Cloudflare Registrar cannot hold a .fr domain (not supported as of 2026-11-19), so DNSSEC DS must be added manually at the external AFNIC registrar; AFNIC 'diffusion restreinte' WHOIS anonymization is automatic for individuals regardless of registrar.

Exact Email Routing MX hostnames are assigned by the dashboard (docs state 'Assigned automatically by Cloudflare' rather than publishing hostnames); the commonly inserted values are route1/route2/route3.mx.cloudflare.net — verify in the dashboard after enabling.

www.cloudflare.com marketing pages (/contact/, /learning/...) returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching; the phone number +1 (650) 319-8930 and the Cloudflare France SAS address were taken from the official privacy policy page instead.

plausible.summary:
Plausible Analytics, verified live Nov 2026:
1) SNIPPET CHANGED Oct 2025: per-site script `https://plausible.io/js/pa-<unique-id>.js` (unique id per site, shown only in your dashboard under Site Settings > Site Installation) + mandatory inline init stub calling `plausible.init()`. Legacy `<script defer data-domain="example.com" src="https://plausible.io/js/script.js"></script>` still works but is legacy; extension variants (script.outbound-links.js etc.) are replaced by `plausible.init({...})` options.
2) Cookieless confirmed: "sets no cookies and writes nothing to local storage or the browser cache". Visitor ID = hash(daily_salt + domain + IP + user_agent); salt rotated and deleted every 24h; raw IP/UA never stored. Data stored in EU (Germany/Falkenstein + Finland, EU-owned infrastructure). Legal entity: Plausible Insights OÜ, Tartu, Estonia.
3) CSP: add `plausible.io` to BOTH script-src (loads /js/pa-*.js) and connect-src (POSTs to https://plausible.io/api/event). No dedicated official CSP page anymore (old /docs/content-security-policy 404s); official guidance lives in /docs/troubleshoot-integration. GOTCHA: the new snippet's inline stub needs a hash/nonce under a strict CSP (or use the legacy no-inline script.js snippet).
4) Minimization: outbound links/file downloads/form submissions toggled off in site settings or via `plausible.init({outboundLinks:false, fileDownloads:false, formSubmissions:false})`. Only localStorage use is the voluntary self-exclusion flag.
5) DPA at https://plausible.io/dpa — auto-accepted by using the service, no signature; references GDPR Art. 28, subprocessor change notifications.
6) Pricing: Starter $9/month (10k pageviews/mo, 1 site, no retention limit), yearly = 2 months free (~$90/yr), 30-day free trial, no credit card.
plausible.details:
CURRENT SNIPPET (new per-site format, Oct 2025+). Exact form, verified character-for-character identical in two independent post-migration deployments; the id part is unique per site and is displayed in Plausible > Site Settings > Site Installation:

<script async src="https://plausible.io/js/pa-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX.js"></script>
<script>
window.plausible=window.plausible||function(){(plausible.q=plausible.q||[]).push(arguments)},plausible.init=plausible.init||function(i){plausible.o=i||{}};
plausible.init()
</script>

Real example id from a live migration: pa-gcQlFlTALeivulBi5cEUe.js (ids are ~21-char base64-ish strings). Place in <head>. Note `async` (new) vs `defer` (old). There is no data-domain attribute anymore — the site identity is baked into the per-site script. plausible.io/docs/plausible-script deliberately does not print the snippet; it says "We display your snippet during the process of adding a new site" (Site Settings > Site installation > Review).

LEGACY SNIPPET (still functional, documented in the script-update-guide as the fallback, e.g. for sending to multiple dashboards):
<script defer data-domain="yourdomain.com" src="https://plausible.io/js/script.js"></script>
This legacy form has NO inline JS — relevant for your strict-CSP static site (see risks).

INIT OPTIONS (plausible.io/docs/script-extensions + /docs/script-update-guide): outboundLinks, fileDownloads, formSubmissions (these three also toggle in dashboard: Site Settings > Tracking > General), hashBasedRouting, autoCapturePageviews, captureOnLocalhost, customProperties, endpoint (replaces the removed data-api attribute). To minimize collection: plausible.init({ outboundLinks:false, fileDownloads:false, formSubmissions:false }). Old data-attribute/extension-filename mechanisms (script.outbound-links.js, script.tagged-events.js, data-api) are no longer supported on the new script.

PRIVACY / DATA (plausible.io/data-policy, /privacy, /dpa):
- "Our script stores nothing on the visitor's device. It sets no cookies and writes nothing to local storage or the browser cache." Only exception: the voluntary opt-out/self-exclusion feature stores a flag in localStorage (user-initiated, e.g. to exclude your own visits).
- Collected: page URLs, referrers, browser/OS/device type, approximate location (country/region/city), pageviews/engagement, custom events/props.
- Visitor identifier: hash(daily_salt + website_domain + ip_address + user_agent); salt rotated and deleted every 24 hours; "Raw IP addresses and User-Agent data are never stored." No cross-day/cross-site tracking.
- Storage: "processed and stored within the European Union on EU-owned infrastructure", servers in Falkenstein, Germany and Finland (Hetzner infrastructure).
- Legal entity: Plausible Insights OÜ, Tartu, Estonia (full registration details on their imprint page).
- DPA: https://plausible.io/dpa — "use of the service constitutes acceptance of this DPA. No separate signature is required." Covers GDPR Art. 28, commits to subprocessor-change notification via in-app/email/blog.

CSP (official guidance, plausible.io/docs/troubleshoot-integration: "add plausible.io to the allowed domains list"; the dedicated docs CSP page was removed — /docs/content-security-policy now 404s):
- script-src: https://plausible.io   (serves /js/pa-*.js)
- connect-src: https://plausible.io  (script POSTs events to https://plausible.io/api/event)
Minimal working form: Content-Security-Policy: ...; script-src 'self' https://plausible.io; connect-src 'self' https://plausible.io
Nothing needed in img-src/style-src/frame-src. No other hosts involved (no CDN).

PRICING (plausible.io homepage pricing section, live): Starter $9/month at 10k monthly pageviews, 1 site, no data-retention limit, goals/custom events, GA import, saved segments, annotations. Yearly billing = 2 months free (pay 10 months, ~$90/yr). Growth $14/mo (3 sites, 3 teammates), Business $19/mo (10 sites, Stats API, funnels). 30-day free trial, no credit card. Prices scale with pageview volume above 10k.
risks: Strict CSP conflict: the NEW snippet requires an inline <script> block (queue stub + plausible.init()). Under a strict script-src without 'unsafe-inline' you must allow it via a CSP hash (sha256-...) or nonce — hash is the practical choice for a static site; recompute it if you ever change the inline block (e.g. add init options). Alternative: keep the legacy one-line script.js snippet, which has zero inline JS and works with plain `script-src https://plausible.io` — but Plausible's verification tool and new features are built around pa-*.js, and extensions-by-filename are deprecated.
The pa-<id>.js snippet is per-site and only obtainable from the Plausible dashboard after creating the site — you cannot hardcode it before signing up; placeholder needed in the repo until then.

The exact inline stub text above was verified from real deployments, not from docs (docs intentionally omit it); after signup, copy the stub exactly as the dashboard shows it, since any whitespace/character difference breaks a CSP hash.

French law note: Plausible sets no cookies, so no CNIL consent banner is required for it; however it is NOT on CNIL's list of formally exempted audience-measurement tools (that list covers configurable tools like Matomo). Mainstream reading: no consent needed (no cookies, no cross-site tracking, EU-hosted) but you should still disclose it in the site's mentions légales/politique de confidentialité, name Plausible Insights OÜ as processor, and link their data policy.

If demos under /demos/<slug>/ run on the same domain, pageviews there count toward the 10k Starter quota and appear in the same dashboard; outbound-link/file-download/form-submission auto-tracking should be toggled off in Site Settings (or via init options) if you want strict minimization — outbound and file-download tracking may be enabled by default in the new setup flow.
data-api attribute no longer works on the new script; a proxy/custom endpoint must use plausible.init({ endpoint: '...' }), which changes the connect-src host accordingly.

Yearly price displayed as '2 months free' on the live site (~$90/yr for Starter); third-party trackers quote it as a 17% discount — verify the exact yearly amount at checkout, and prices increase in steps above 10k pageviews/month.

legal.summary:
1) Mentions légales: confirmed — the obligation now sits in art. 1-1 of loi n°2004-575 (LCEN), rewritten by loi SREN n°2024-449 (in force 23 May 2024), Légifrance id LEGIARTI000049568614. Art. 1-1 II lets a non-professional editor stay anonymous by publishing ONLY the host's name/denomination and address, "sous réserve d'avoir communiqué à ce fournisseur les éléments d'identification personnelle mentionnés au I" (nom, prénoms, domicile, téléphone). Nothing obliges a non-professional who voluntarily shows his name to add address/phone (those are I-regime items), but the law is silent on mixing — see risks. Host info under the general regime (I, 4°): name, address AND phone.
2) CNIL audience measurement: exemption rests on art. 82 loi 78-17 + lignes directrices délib. n°2020-091 du 17/09/2020 + recommandation 2020-092. The named list of exempted solutions IS GONE: since 04/07/2025 the CNIL page "Cookies : solutions pour les outils de mesure d'audience" replaces it with a provider self-assessment PDF ("Outil d'auto-évaluation relatif à la mise en œuvre d'une solution de mesure d'audience exemptée de consentement"). Criteria verified (archived official page, snapshot 01/01/2026): sole-purpose audience measurement for the publisher's exclusive account, anonymous statistics only, no cross-referencing/transmission of non-anonymous data to third parties, no cross-site tracking; recommended: 13-month tracker life (not auto-renewed), 25-month max retention, periodic review, user information via privacy policy. Plausible passes every criterion and, storing nothing on the device (no cookies, no localStorage), arguably doesn't even trigger art. 82.
3) localStorage game saves (never transmitted): exempt from consent under art. 82 al. final, 2° ("strictement nécessaire à la fourniture d'un service... à la demande expresse de l'utilisateur"); délib. 2020-091 art. 1 expressly covers "le local storage mis en œuvre au sein du standard HTML 5"; transparency still required — describe it in the privacy policy.
4) EU→US: DPF adequacy decision (EU) 2023/1795 still in force as of Nov 2026. General Court dismissed Latombe, T-553/23, 3 Sept 2025 (CP 106/25); appeal C-703/25 P filed 31 Oct 2025, pending — no CJEU ruling yet. Cloudflare, Inc. states certification under EU-U.S. DPF + Swiss DPF + UK Extension in its privacy policy, with SCCs as fallback in its DPA; it acts as processor for customer logs; retention "for a limited period" (no public fixed figure).
5) AFNIC: yes — restricted diffusion of WHOIS data is automatic/by default for natural persons on .fr (since 2006); technical data stay published; disclosure only on legitimate request per the Charte de nommage.
6) Dual licensing: keep LICENSE as pure MIT (GitHub/Licensee detection breaks on mixed files) and put the content carve-out in README — exact wording provided in details.
legal.details:
## 1. Mentions légales — art. 1-1 LCEN (post-SREN)

Source: https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/article_lc/LEGIARTI000049568614 — "Modifié par LOI n°2024-449 du 21 mai 2024", "en vigueur depuis le 23 mai 2024". The content of ex-art. 6 III LCEN was moved here by the loi SREN n°2024-449 du 21 mai 2024.

Structure verified on Légifrance:
- I (all editors, chapeau has NO "à titre professionnel" restriction): "Les personnes dont l'activité est d'éditer un service de communication au public en ligne mettent à la disposition du public, dans un standard ouvert :"
  - 1° personnes physiques: "leurs nom, prénoms, domicile et numéro de téléphone" + RCS/RNE number if applicable;
  - 2° personnes morales: dénomination/raison sociale, siège, téléphone, registration, capital;
  - 3° name of the directeur de la publication (and responsable de la rédaction if any);
  - 4° "Le nom, la dénomination ou la raison sociale, l'adresse et le numéro de téléphone du fournisseur de services d'hébergement";
  - 5° persons storing data for the service, where applicable.
- II (non-professional carve-out), verbatim: "Les personnes éditant à titre non professionnel un service de communication au public en ligne peuvent ne tenir à la disposition du public, pour préserver leur anonymat, que le nom, la dénomination ou la raison sociale et l'adresse du fournisseur de services d'hébergement, sous réserve d'avoir communiqué à ce fournisseur les éléments d'identification personnelle mentionnés au I." The host is bound by professional secrecy over those elements (disclosure only to judicial authorities).
- The article also carries the droit de réponse (3-month window, insertion within 3 days, 3 750 € fine) and a criminal sanction of up to one year's imprisonment and 75 000 € fine (375 000 € / dissolution-range penalties for legal persons, cf. C. pén. 131-38/131-39) for breach of the I–II obligations.

Answers:
- A non-professional may lawfully publish ONLY: host name/denomination + host address (phone not required by II's minimal set, but I-4° includes it — publish it anyway, it costs nothing and removes ambiguity), PROVIDED he has transmitted nom, prénoms, domicile, téléphone to the host.
- If he voluntarily displays his NAME: the LCEN does not say he thereby loses the II derogation; II defines the minimum made available to the public, and exceeding the minimum is not prohibited. The strict fallback reading (full I regime incl. domicile+phone once you don't claim anonymity) has no textual anchor for non-professionals who still keep ID on file with the host, but it is doctrinally untested — see risks.
- Practical mentions légales block (non-professional, name shown voluntarily): "Site édité à titre non professionnel (art. 1-1, II, loi n°2004-575 du 21 juin 2004). Éditeur : [Prénom Nom] — les éléments d'identification personnelle ont été communiqués à l'hébergeur. Directeur de la publication : l'éditeur. Hébergeur : Cloudflare, Inc., 101 Townsend St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA — tél. +1 888 993 5273 (vérifier)."

## 2. CNIL audience measurement exemption

Legal basis: art. 82 loi n°78-17 (verified live, https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/article_lc/LEGIARTI000037813978, en vigueur): consent required for any read/write on the terminal, except when it "a pour finalité exclusive de permettre ou faciliter la communication par voie électronique" or "est strictement nécessaire à la fourniture d'un service de communication en ligne à la demande expresse de l'utilisateur".
Interpretation: délibération n°2020-091 du 17 septembre 2020 (lignes directrices, Légifrance CNILTEXT000042398005) + recommandation n°2020-092 du 17 septembre 2020.

Current criteria — official CNIL page "Cookies : solutions pour les outils de mesure d'audience", dated 04 juillet 2025 (cnil.fr was in maintenance on 2026-11-19; read via Wayback snapshot of 2026-01-01, https://web.archive.org/web/20260101103334/https://www.cnil.fr/fr/cookies-solutions-pour-les-outils-de-mesure-daudience):
MUST: (a) purpose strictly limited to audience measurement of the site/app (performance measurement, navigation-problem detection, technical/ergonomic optimization, server capacity estimation, analysis of content consulted) "pour le compte exclusif de l'éditeur"; (b) produce "des données statistiques anonymes uniquement".
MUST NOT: (c) cross-reference the data with other processing or pass non-anonymous data to third parties; (d) allow cross-site/cross-app tracking of the person (any shared identifier across sites, e.g. third-party-domain cookies for unified reach, is excluded).
RECOMMENDED: inform users (privacy policy is given as the example vehicle); tracker lifetime capped so audiences stay comparable, "comme c'est le cas d'une durée de treize mois", not auto-extended on new visits; collected info kept max "vingt-cinq mois"; periodic review of both durations.
List of exempted solutions: REMOVED (believed correctly). The page now offers providers an "outil d'auto-évaluation" (PDF, 241.43 Ko, "Outil d'auto-évaluation relatif à la mise en œuvre d'une solution de mesure d'audience exemptée de consentement") detailing sufficient conditions; providers meeting them may state (CNIL's suggested wording): "D'après notre auto-évaluation, la solution XXX est conforme aux critères établis par la CNIL... peut être mise en œuvre sans requérir le consentement... si elle est correctement configurée" — but may NOT claim CNIL certification/validation or use its logo. Publishers are told to ask providers for the justification documents. Press coverage (ppc.land) adds the tool's technical details (first-party only, IP truncation after coarse geolocation, aggregation ~10 users, 13/25-month caps).

Plausible vs each criterion (source: https://plausible.io/data-policy):
- (a) sole purpose/publisher's account: "You retain full ownership and control of your website data"; data shared only with subprocessors needed to run the service → OK (Plausible = processor).
- (b) anonymous statistics: dashboard is aggregate; visitor identifier = hash(daily_salt + domain + IP + UA), salt rotated and deleted every 24h; "Raw IP addresses and User-Agent data are never stored" → OK.
- (c) no cross-referencing / no third-party transmission of non-anonymous data: "We do not sell your data"; EU-only infrastructure ("All visitor data is securely processed and stored in the EU... Visitor data does not leave the EU") → OK.
- (d) no cross-site tracking: "We do not track people across devices, websites or apps. The daily visitor identifier is specific to a single website and device." → OK.
- 13-month tracker life: N/A — "Our script stores nothing on the visitor's device. It sets no cookies and writes nothing to local storage or the browser cache." Since art. 82 governs terminal read/write, a storage-less tool arguably never triggers the consent rule at all; the exemption analysis is belt-and-braces.
- 25-month retention: applies to non-anonymous collected info; Plausible's identifiers die daily and stats are aggregate — ask Plausible for its CNIL self-assessment documentation to close this point (accountability).
GDPR side (independent of art. 82): transient IP/UA processing = personal data processing; basis = intérêt légitime (art. 6(1)(f)) of the publisher in measuring audience; mention it in the privacy policy.

## 3. localStorage for game saves/preferences

Délib. 2020-091, art. 1 scope covers "les cookies HTTP... ainsi que d'autres technologies telles que les local shared objects..., le local storage mis en œuvre au sein du standard HTML 5, les identifications par calcul d'empreinte...". Art. 5 exempts trackers strictly necessary to the service expressly requested, with examples including cart memory and "personnalisation de l'interface utilisateur (choix de la langue ou de la présentation)". A purely local game save/preferences store, never transmitted, fits art. 82, 2° exactly. No consent banner needed. Transparency remains due: privacy policy should state — what is stored (localStorage keys for game progress and settings), purpose (resume games, keep preferences), strictly local (never sent to any server, not readable by third parties), retention (until the user clears site data or uses the in-game reset), deletion method (browser settings "effacer les données de site" or in-game button), and legal ground (exempt from consent, art. 82 loi 78-17, strictly necessary to the service requested).

## 4. EU→US transfers, Nov 2026

- Adequacy decision: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795 of 10 July 2023 (DPF) — in force.
- Tribunal (General Court), case T-553/23 Latombe v Commission, judgment of 3 September 2025 (press release CP 106/25, curia.europa.eu): action dismissed; DPRC held sufficiently independent; US bulk-collection safeguards adequate at decision date.
- Appeal to the CJEU: C-703/25 P, lodged 31 October 2025, pending, no hearing date — the DPF therefore remains valid but under challenge ("Schrems III" risk).
- Cloudflare: privacy policy (https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/): "Cloudflare has certified to the U.S. Department of Commerce that it adheres to the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework Principles", plus Swiss-U.S. DPF and UK Extension; trust hub (https://www.cloudflare.com/trust-hub/gdpr/): relies on DPF for EEA/CH/UK→US transfers, and on SCCs "including supplementary measures as necessary" via its standard DPA (incorporated into the Self-Serve Subscription Agreement); role: "data processor of Customer Logs..."; metadata (chiefly IPs) processed "for a limited period of time" — no public fixed retention figure for CDN logs.
- Privacy-policy paragraph (adapt): "Hébergement et journaux techniques — Ce site est servi par Cloudflare, Inc. (USA). Lors de votre visite, Cloudflare traite des données techniques (adresse IP, user-agent, métadonnées de requête, journaux de sécurité) afin d'acheminer le site, d'assurer sa sécurité (anti-DDoS, pare-feu) et ses performances. Base légale : intérêt légitime de l'éditeur (art. 6.1.f RGPD) à la fourniture sûre du site. Cloudflare agit en qualité de sous-traitant (DPA Cloudflare). Transferts hors UE : Cloudflare, Inc. est certifiée au titre du Data Privacy Framework UE-États-Unis (décision d'adéquation (UE) 2023/1795 du 10 juillet 2023) et applique en complément les clauses contractuelles types. Les journaux sont conservés par Cloudflare pour une durée limitée conformément à sa politique de confidentialité ; l'éditeur n'accède pas aux journaux bruts."

## 5. AFNIC .fr WHOIS

Yes — automatic. AFNIC expert paper (https://www.afnic.fr/en/observatory-and-resources/expert-papers/personal-data-are-published-in-the-whois-online-directory-is-this-normal/): for natural persons "the contact details of the holder are protected by confidentiality by default" ("diffusion restreinte"), a mechanism in place since 2006 for .fr (and .re/.tf/.yt/.pm/.wf); technical data (registrar, DNS servers, technical contact) remain published; AFNIC discloses identity only "on legitimate request" under the Charte de nommage framework (current edition: afnic-charte-de-nommage-06-07-2026.pdf on afnic.fr). No action needed by an individual holder; nothing to pay, nothing to request.

## 6. Dual licensing (MIT code / all-rights-reserved content)

GitHub docs (https://docs.github.com/.../licensing-a-repository): a repo without a license ⇒ "the default copyright laws apply... no one may reproduce, distribute, or create derivative works"; for mixed licensing GitHub advises: "simplify your LICENSE file and note the complexity somewhere else, such as your repository's README file."
Recommended layout:
- LICENSE — the unmodified MIT text only (keeps Licensee/GitHub detection working): "Copyright (c) 2026 [Name]" + standard MIT body.
- README section:
  "## License
  The source code of this repository (HTML/CSS/JS, build scripts, demo game code) is licensed under the MIT License — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
  The following are NOT covered by the MIT License and are © 2026 [Name], all rights reserved: all texts, images, photographs, graphics, the CV, and any personal data contained in this repository or on the website. They may not be reproduced, distributed, or reused without prior written permission."
  French mirror for the site footer: "Code source sous licence MIT — Textes, images et CV © 2026 [Nom], tous droits réservés."
- Optionally add a one-line header in content directories (e.g. /assets/NOTICE.txt) repeating the carve-out.

## Owner's verification checklist
1. Re-read art. 1-1 live on Légifrance (link above) before publishing — confirm no amendment after Nov 2026; confirm the sanction paragraph as displayed.
2. Ensure full identification (nom, prénoms, domicile, téléphone) is accurately on file with BOTH the registrar and Cloudflare (account data) — this is the express condition of the II anonymity regime.
3. Verify Cloudflare's exact legal name/postal address/phone for the mentions légales on an official Cloudflare page before go-live.
4. When cnil.fr exits maintenance: re-read "Cookies : solutions pour les outils de mesure d'audience" live and download the "Outil d'auto-évaluation" PDF; request Plausible's self-assessment/justification documentation and archive it (accountability, art. 5(2) RGPD).
5. Check Cloudflare's ACTIVE status on https://www.dataprivacyframework.gov/ participant search (JS app — manual check required; automated fetch could not list it).
6. Monitor CJEU case C-703/25 P (curia.europa.eu); if the DPF falls, the Cloudflare DPA's SCCs become the transfer basis — update the privacy policy then.
7. Confirm the WHOIS of the actual .fr domain shows restricted diffusion (run a whois query) and skim the current Charte de nommage section on data publication.
8. CSP: allow the Plausible script and event endpoint (script-src/connect-src https://plausible.io) and confirm the EU-hosted plan; if self-hosting, none of this is needed.
9. Decide name display: safest = II regime alone (host details only); name + II regime is defensible but doctrinally untested — accept the residual uncertainty consciously.
10. Keep LICENSE file pure MIT; carve-out only in README/footer, or GitHub's license detection may misreport.
risks: cnil.fr was fully in maintenance on 2026-11-19 ('Le site de la CNIL est actuellement en maintenance'): the audience-measurement criteria were verified on a Wayback snapshot (2026-01-01) of the official page dated 04/07/2025 — re-verify live and download the auto-évaluation PDF once the site is back

CNIL no longer whitelists tools: Plausible's exemption rests on the provider's self-assessment, not CNIL validation; obtain and archive Plausible's documentation, and re-check after any Plausible feature change (e.g. funnels/props could alter the analysis)

Mixing regimes (showing one's name while withholding address/phone under art. 1-1 II) is not expressly settled by the text or case law — defensible since II only fixes the public minimum, but a strict reading of I exists; safest is host-details-only
Art. 1-1 II's minimal set omits the host's phone number while I-4° requires it — publish the host's phone as well to be safe
DPF under appeal (CJEU C-703/25 P, lodged 31 Oct 2025): a 'Schrems III' invalidation would require switching the privacy policy's transfer basis to the SCCs in Cloudflare's DPA
Cloudflare publishes no fixed retention period for CDN/security logs ('limited period of time') — the privacy policy cannot state a precise duration and should not invent one

Criminal exposure exists for defective mentions légales (up to 1 year / 75 000 €): the anonymity regime only protects if identity was actually transmitted to the host — stale or incomplete account data at Cloudflare/registrar would void it
Strict security headers: CSP must whitelist plausible.io (script-src + connect-src) or analytics silently breaks; test after deploying headers
If any future demo/game writes identifiers to localStorage that ARE transmitted (scores, telemetry), the art. 82 exemption analysis must be redone for that feature
Putting the dual-license carve-out inside the LICENSE file breaks GitHub/Licensee detection — keep it in README only

claudecode.summary:
In Claude Code (late 2026), the **recommended format is Skills**: `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`.

The older `.claude/commands/<name>.md` format still works for backward compatibility but is legacy.

**Skills file layout**: `~/.claude/skills/nouveau-projet/SKILL.md` plus optional supporting files (reference.md, examples.md, scripts/).

**Key frontmatter fields**:
- `name`: Command name (defaults to directory name; yours would be `nouveau-projet`)
- `description`: When Claude should use it (1,536 char limit combined with `when_to_use`)
- `arguments`: [array of named positional args] for `$name` substitution
- `argument-hint`: "[hint]" for / menu autocomplete
- `allowed-tools`: "Read Grep Write" (pre-approve without prompts)
- `paths`: Glob patterns limiting when skill auto-activates
- `model`, `effort`, `context`: Override session settings

**Argument passing**:
- `$0`, `$1`, `$2`... (0-indexed positional)
- `$name` (named from `arguments` field)
- `$ARGUMENTS` (all args as typed)
- `${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}`, `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`, `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` (env-like)

**Example invocation**: `/nouveau-projet "my project" typescript` with `arguments: [name, language]` expands `$name` → "my project", `$language` → typescript.
claudecode.details:
From https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md (fetched 2026-11-19):

**File layout**:
```
~/.claude/skills/nouveau-projet/
├── SKILL.md (required frontmatter + markdown)
├── reference.md (optional)
├── examples.md (optional)
└── scripts/ (optional)
```

**Frontmatter template**:
```yaml
---
name: nouveau-projet
description: Create a new project with scaffolding
argument-hint: "[project-name] [language]"
arguments: [name, language]
allowed-tools: "Read Write Bash Glob"
paths: "src/**/*.ts,config/**/*.json"
---
```

**Content**: Markdown with shell command injection via `!`...backticks:
```markdown
# Nouveau Projet

!`echo Creating $name in $language`

## Setup
Create directory: $0
```

**Backward compat**: `.claude/commands/deploy.md` still loads as `/deploy`. Commands support all frontmatter fields *except* `name` and `paths`. Skills (the preferred format) support the full feature set including supporting files and glob-based activation.

**Argument rules**:
- Indexed: `$0`, `$1` stay literal if no arg provided
- Named: `$name` expands to empty string if missing
- Multi-word args require quotes: `/nouveau-projet "my app" node`
- All args: `$ARGUMENTS`
risks: Shell injection in frontmatter commands (dynamic context injection) if `disableSkillShellExecution` is not set and you pass untrusted input
Skill content stays in context across turns after first invocation—be aware of token accumulation
Commands format lacks `name` and `paths` frontmatter support—use skills for new work
